description: Cult sci-fi surf-rock instrumentalists Man or Astro-man? play their famously theatrical live show, with Atlanta garage band The Subsonics. All ages, doors 8pm.

title: Bachata Tuesday Class & Social (last Tuesday)
description: A monthly bachata night: a 7pm class (intermediate-leaning) with Bryon & Samm, then social dancing to DJ Thiencito until 11. No partner required.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The year's last Woodchopper's Ball at the Verdi Club: live swing band, a drop-in beginner lesson 9-9:15pm, and no partner needed.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: The nightly HellaFunny stand-up showcase at The Function, a cheap night out in the quiet week between Christmas and New Year. 4-5 comics, 70-90 minutes, 21+, with a two-drink minimum.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance (5th Wednesday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Andy Shore and live music from Christopher Jacoby and Corey Walters. The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: BACDS New Year's Eve Contra Ball
venue: First United Methodist Church of Palo Alto
description: A four-hour New Year's Eve contra ball with caller Susan Petrick and fiddle and guitar from Will Wheeler and Ben Jackson. It's the most ceilidh-like way to see in the new year. Palo Alto is about an hour by Caltrain from 4th & King, so check the late trains home.

title: The Lemon Twigs New Year's Eve, with Tchotchke
description: The D'Addario brothers' '60s/'70s-style power-pop band ring in 2027 in the Chapel's converted mortuary hall, with Tchotchke and a DJ. All ages, standing.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night: New Year's Day show
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($25 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A low-key New Year's Day night out: the HellaFunny nightly stand-up showcase at The Function on Market St. There's also a 9pm show; 21+.

title: The Board Walks: Walk & Talk About Life's Big Questions
description: A weekly 5-mile walking conversation club for people who want depth over small talk. Everyone brings a question to explore, shares it in an opening circle, then drifts between small conversations on the walk. It's newcomer-friendly and runs rain or shine.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Castro, Tales of the Village
address: Castro St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94114
description: A free volunteer-led two-hour history walk through the Castro, from Harvey Milk's camera-shop campaign to how the neighbourhood keeps evolving. It starts at Jane Warner Plaza.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. Partners rotate, so you don't need to bring one. Weather permitting.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: New Year's first-Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then salsa and mambo dancing until 11:30. A good fresh-start night out.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: The first SalsaCrazy Monday of 2027 (and the start of the January progressive series). A beginner salsa lesson with no partner needed, then salsa and bachata dancing at a real club. 21+.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st and 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers and hosts rotate; the SF CI WhatsApp group posts who's on. First Monday after New Year — confirm it's running in the SF CI WhatsApp group before going.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). New monthly Lindy Hop and Balboa class series usually start the first Tuesday of the month (7-9pm, before the dance). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20-$30 at door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A midweek stand-up showcase with 4-5 local comics at The Function on Market St.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Doe Taryn and live music from Leah Wollenberg and Jeremy Reinhard. The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: The Loved Ones: Latest Hits record release, with The Vesuvians
description: The '90s Bay Area mod/R&B band (singer Bart Davenport, Cake's Xan McCurdy) celebrates a new record, with The Vesuvians featuring Karina Deniké and DJ Russell Quan. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: La Hora Feliz: Friday Spanish conversation meetup
description: A relaxed weekly all-Spanish conversation hour for learners and native speakers at a Valencia St cafe. There's no cover. Newcomers are told to arrive around 6:30pm and ask at the counter for the group.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey in 70mm
description: Kubrick's masterpiece on a 70mm print in the restored 1922 Castro Theatre, a start-of-year big-screen event. All ages; doors 7pm. The ticket price is behind TicketWeb's bot wall.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Welcome to San Francisco (for newcomers)
venue: Harry Bridges Plaza (across from the Ferry Building)
address: The Embarcadero at Market St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A volunteer-led two-hour introductory walk designed for people new to the city. It goes from the Ferry Building to North Beach, covering the Gold Rush, cable cars, the 1906 quake, counterculture and food culture, and ends near North Beach cafes.

title: Anna von Hausswolff with KatzPascale
description: The Swedish singer and organist plays towering, cathedral-sized drone-pop. The List marks it 'sold out', but the official ticket page was still selling GA tickets on Oct 30. Mostly standing; doors 7pm.

title: Swirlies with Seko
description: The Boston shoegaze and indie-rock cult band at the Chapel (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7pm.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with Hep Jen's free beginner lesson at noon. No partner or experience is needed. It's weather permitting, so check the site that morning in January.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Embarcadero South, A Turbulent Port
venue: Mission & Steuart Streets, by Rincon Center (meeting point)
address: Mission St & Steuart St, San Francisco, CA 94105
description: A free two-hour waterfront history walk starting a few blocks from home. It covers the 150-year-old seawall, the Hills Bros. Coffee building, Rincon Annex and the 1934 longshore strike memorials, on the stretch where the Embarcadero Freeway once stood.

title: Nora Brown with Stephanie Coleman
description: Young Brooklyn banjo player Nora Brown, one of the most acclaimed voices in Appalachian old-time music, with fiddler Stephanie Coleman. An intimate folkYEAH! show; all ages, doors 7pm.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata social
description: A long-running Monday salsa night: a beginner lesson at 7pm (no partner or experience needed), intermediate at 7:45, then salsa and bachata social dancing from 8:30. 21+.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: LSD and the Search for God with Cryogeyser
description: The cult shoegaze band plays a rare headline set, with dream-pop band Cryogeyser in support. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: Weekly Friday bachata (sensual/fusion) with concurrent beginner, intermediate and advanced classes from 8pm, partners rotating every minute. Social dancing runs 9:30pm-1am.

title: The 16th Annual Bowie Bash
description: The 16th annual Bowie birthday-month bash: a costumed Bowie tribute band (billed on The List as the First Church of the Sacred Silversexual) plus drag, burlesque and puppetry, in a room built for dancing. Night one of two (Sat Jan 16 too); doors 8pm.

title: Social & Economic Justice Music and the Arts Festival: evening concert
description: A one-day festival at the historic Victoria Theatre bringing musicians, poets and community organisers together. Workshops run 9am-7pm, then an all-genres concert at 7pm.

title: The 16th Annual Bowie Bash (night 2: Band Picks)
description: Night two of GAMH's annual Bowie birthday-month bash, where Bowie tribute band the First Church of the Sacred Silversexual plays the band's own favourite Bowie songs. Doors 8pm, show 9:30pm.

title: Laser cutter safety training at Noisebridge
description: A two-hour hands-on class on the hackerspace's 150W CO2 laser cutter, covering hazards, safe operation and fire response. Everyone cuts a cardboard piece, and it's the prerequisite for using the cutter on your own projects. Seats are limited.

title: Mucha Salsa+ social (free beginner class)
description: A not-for-profit Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club. Beginner and intermediate salsa classes run 7-8pm and are included, then there's DJ social dancing until 11:30pm, so it's easy to come solo.

title: Tara Clerkin Trio
description: The Bristol trio's hazy, hypnotic mix of avant-folk, dub-tinged jazz and chamber pop, co-presented by KALW in a 350-cap room on an MLK Day evening. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: January's in-person drop-in circling and authentic relating evening from The Circling Institute, open to newcomers. Register ahead: doors 6:45pm and close at 7:10pm sharp. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: True Widow
description: The Dallas trio's slow, heavy 'stonegaze' (shoegaze meets stoner rock, with boy/girl vocals) in the ornate Tenderloin music hall. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance (The Flagstones)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Charlie Fenton and live band The Flagstones (Anne Goess, Charlie Hancock, Will Wheeler). The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic sprung dance floor. It's a social dance for those who already know some tango, and also a good place to watch and meet the local scene.

title: Eliane Elias Quartet: Antônio Carlos Jobim Centennial Celebration
description: The Brazilian pianist-singer marks 100 years of Tom Jobim with a bossa nova programme in SFJAZZ's main hall. Runs Jan 22-24, and the Sunday is 'The Art of Bossa Nova'.

title: Fruition: Something More, The Final Tour, with Rainbow Girls
description: The Portland string-band-turned-rock group's farewell tour, with Bay Area harmony trio Rainbow Girls opening. All ages; doors 8pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Golden Gate Park, West End
venue: North (Dutch) Windmill, Queen Wilhelmina Garden (meeting point)
address: JFK Dr at Great Highway, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A free volunteer-led walk at the ocean end of Golden Gate Park, from the Dutch Windmill past the Murphy Windmill to the Beach Chalet's 1930s murals. It covers how the sand dunes were turned into parkland and a dune village built from retired cable cars.

title: The Brothers Comatose
description: SF's own rowdy five-piece string band plays bluegrass, country and rock 'n' roll at full volume, one of the most fun live nights in town. Night two of two (Fri Jan 22 too). All ages; doors 8:30pm.

title: Irish trad seisiún at the Plough and Stars
description: The weekly Sunday-afternoon instrumental Irish session at SF's best-known trad pub. Come to listen, or bring an instrument and join in.

title: Gerald Henig: Little-Known (and Shocking) Revelations About America's Presidents
description: Cal State East Bay historian Gerald Henig shares funny, tragic and bizarre stories from his award-finalist book America's Presidents: What Your History Teacher Never Told You, on why so few presidents achieved greatness. In-person only.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: A beginner salsa lesson (no partner or experience required), then salsa and bachata social dancing at the Inner Richmond's long-running Monday dance night. 21+.

title: Bebel Gilberto: 25 Years of Tanto Tempo
description: The Brazilian singer marks 25 years of her electronic bossa-nova classic Tanto Tempo. Doors 7pm, 21+; on sale Fri 11/6.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Jon Bryant
description: Canadian indie-folk singer-songwriter Jon Bryant previews his back-to-roots album Harbour in the 1907 basement speakeasy. Tickets are 'on sale soon' as of Oct 30; 21+, doors 7pm.

title: BD in the YUniverse: BD Wong performs Charles Yu stories
description: Tony winner and SF native BD Wong performs four funny, moving short stories by National Book Award winner Charles Yu. Four performances only, Jan 28-31, in A.C.T.'s experimental ACTivate series.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic sprung dance floor. It's a social dance for those who already know some tango, and also a good place to watch and meet the local scene.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: Beginner, intermediate and advanced bachata classes at 8pm with constant partner rotation, then a social until 1am. A very easy place to meet people.

title: Ty Segall
description: The prolific garage-rock hero, an SF scene alumnus, in a small room: the first of two nights at the Chapel (Sat Jan 30 too). All ages; doors 7:30pm.

title: Stamptown at SF Sketchfest 2027, hosted by Zach Zucker
description: Zach Zucker's chaotic, character-heavy alt-comedy showcase, one of the first SF Sketchfest 2027 shows on sale. The festival runs Jan 14-31, and its initial lineup drops Nov 13. 18+; doors 6pm.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. Partners rotate, so you don't need to bring one. Weather permitting.

title: Vansire with Eliza McLamb
description: The Minnesota dream-pop duo Vansire, with indie songwriter Eliza McLamb, at Bimbo's. Doors 7pm, all ages; price per The List.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance on the Verdi Club's 2,500 sq ft floor. The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Cécile McLorin Salvant
description: The Grammy-winning jazz vocalist opens a four-night SFJAZZ run (Feb 4-7). The cheapest seats ($50) fit the budget.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: The first-Sunday salsa night at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then salsa and mambo social dancing. Easy to come solo.

title: Fat Tuesday Celebration with Rebirth Brass Band
description: New Orleans' Rebirth Brass Band plays Mardi Gras night, with NOLA food and drink specials and the East Bay Brass Band in the Curio bar. Doors 7pm.

title: 16th Annual Salsa Rueda Festival
description: A four-day Cuban salsa and rueda festival (Thu-Sun) with 60+ workshops, a beginner bootcamp and nightly parties with bands and DJs. Buy a party pass to keep within budget.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic floor, a good night to watch and meet the local tango scene.

title: Lael Neale with Spacemoth (solo)
description: Sub Pop's Lael Neale plays her hypnotic, omnichord-driven indie folk (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7:30pm.

title: Richard Thompson & Band with Clayton Linthicum and Quinn Bachand
description: The Fairport Convention co-founder and British folk-rock guitar legend plays a seated show with his band. Doors 7pm; price per The List.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson (Valentine's Day)
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson at noon. No partner needed; weather permitting.

title: Hello! Bachata & Kizomba Sunday (Valentine's Day)
description: A daytime bachata social (and kizomba upstairs) on the Verdi Club's two floors on Valentine's Day. Social, easy to join solo, and over by evening.

title: Jess Williamson with Andrew Sa (Noise Pop 2027)
description: The Texan singer-songwriter's country-tinged indie folk, on the opening night of Noise Pop 2027 (Feb 18-28). Doors 7pm.

title: Fink with Maggie Koerner
description: Fin Greenall's Fink plays his 1974-style folk album The City Is Coming to Erase It All, with New Orleans singer Maggie Koerner. Doors 8:30pm; price per The List.

title: San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade (Year of the Ram)
address: Second St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105
description: The big Lunar New Year night parade of dragons, lion dancers, floats and drummers, stepping off at 2nd & Market a few minutes from home. Chinatown's Community Street Fair runs the same weekend (Sat-Sun Feb 20-21) on Grant Ave.

title: Mucha Salsa+ social (free beginner class)
description: A not-for-profit Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club. Beginner and intermediate classes run 7-8pm and are included, then DJ social dancing until 11:30pm.

title: Cut Worms (solo) (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Max Clarke's Cut Worms plays a solo set of Everly Brothers-flavoured indie folk-pop in the Swedish American Hall, as part of Noise Pop 2027.

title: Sylvie
description: LA band Sylvie's warm, '70s-style Laurel Canyon soft rock and folk (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Deerhoof with Earthball and Gumby's Junk
description: SF-born art-rock band Deerhoof plays a hometown show at the Great American Music Hall. Doors 7pm.

title: Timnit Gebru: The Rise of AI and the Radicalization of a Tech Idealist
description: The AI-ethics researcher, who left Google's Ethical AI team after warning about large language models, talks about her career and the AI industry. Doors 6:30pm.

title: Asaf Avidan: Into the Great Abyss solo tour
description: The gravel-voiced Israeli singer-songwriter plays a solo show of folk, blues and jazz-tinged songs. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Here We Go Magic: 15th Anniversary of A Different Ship (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Luke Temple's Brooklyn indie band revisits its Nigel Godrich-produced album A Different Ship, as part of Noise Pop. Doors 7pm.

title: Upswing Series: Tyreek McDole / Isaiah Collier
description: A double bill in Terence Blanchard's rising-stars series: vocalist Tyreek McDole and spiritual-jazz saxophonist Isaiah Collier.

title: Caroline Rose: Uncle Carol's World of Fun Tour (Noise Pop 2027)
description: The genre-hopping indie songwriter plays the Castro Theatre for Noise Pop 2027. Doors 7pm, all ages; price per The List.
